## CJS и ESM с точки зрения сборщика

Сами системы модулей — `require` против `import`, live bindings, порядок выполнения — разобраны в топике Node.js, в главе про CommonJS и ESM.
worst_places.problem: ESM is used 118 times and CJS 92 times across the 18 files of this zone, and neither is ever expanded once — not here, not anywhere. This heading is the single place where the binding was unavoidable: the heading says CJS, the very next sentence says CommonJS, and the text still never states that they are the same word. A reader who does not already know the letters has to infer the mapping from adjacency, and for ESM there is no adjacent hint at all. Half of this topic rests on the distinction, so the acronym gap is not cosmetic.

worst_places.after:
## CJS и ESM с точки зрения сборщика

Два сокращения, которые дальше встречаются на каждом шагу. **CJS — это CommonJS**, модульная система Node.js с `require` и `module.exports`. **ESM — это ECMAScript Modules**, модули самого языка с `import` и `export`. Сами системы модулей — `require` против `import`, live bindings, порядок выполнения — разобраны в топике Node.js, в главе про CommonJS и ESM. Здесь важно ровно одно свойство и его последствия для сборки.

worst_places.quote: Конкретно: **CJS-зависимость** жила в dev за счёт пребандлинга, а в проде дала `does not provide an export named` или пустой объект; **стили пропали** из-за `sideEffects: false` и тришейкинга; **`process is not defined`** — в браузере это Node API, нужен `import.meta.env`; **другой порядок инициализации** — объединение модулей меняет порядок, и цикл в графе, безобидный в dev, ломается в проде; **ошибки типов доехали до прода** — Vite вообще не проверяет типы, он их вырезает, поэтому `tsc --noEmit` обязан быть отдельным шагом CI; **ассет не нашёлся** — путь собирался строкой и не был переписан при сборке.
worst_places.problem: One ~95-word sentence carrying six independent failure modes joined by semicolons, each with its own cause and its own fix. Six unfamiliar things stack up with nothing to hold on to, and on a phone this is a single unbroken block. Article 06 presents exactly this content as a three-column table (симптом / причина / как поймать заранее) — so the readable form already exists in the zone and was flattened here. This is also the only file in the zone with no table or diagram at all.

worst_places.after:
У всех причин один корень: dev и prod выполняют разный код, и dev проверяет меньше, чем кажется. Шесть типичных случаев:

- **CJS-зависимость** жила в dev за счёт пребандлинга, а в проде дала `does not provide an export named` или пустой объект.
- **Стили пропали** из-за `sideEffects: false` вместе с тришейкингом.
- **`process is not defined`** — в браузере `process` не существует, это Node API; нужен `import.meta.env`.
- **Другой порядок инициализации** — объединение модулей меняет порядок, и цикл в графе, безобидный в dev, ломается в проде.
- **Ошибки типов доехали до прода** — Vite вообще не проверяет типы, он их вырезает. Поэтому `tsc --noEmit` обязан быть отдельным шагом в CI.
- **Ассет не нашёлся** — путь к файлу собирался строкой и не был переписан при сборке.

Практический вывод один: прод-сборка должна выполняться в CI на каждый pull request, а перед релизом её результат стоит открыть локально.

worst_places.quote: The fix takes two parts at once: handling the error in the application (catch it, retry once, reload the page on a second failure) and handling it at deploy time (do not delete the previous release's assets immediately; keep several versions around).
worst_places.problem: 42 words, one colon, two nested parentheticals, and a bare gerund pair ("handling ... and handling") as the grammatical spine. The reader has to hold the split open across both brackets to see that these are two places, not two steps. The Russian original is 28 words for the same four facts — this is the clearest single instance of the zone-wide pattern where a comfortable RU sentence becomes an over-limit EN one because the translation keeps the RU colon-and-parenthesis chaining and then adds ~19% more words on top.
worst_places.before: The fix takes two parts at once: handling the error in the application (catch it, retry once, reload the page on a second failure) and handling it at deploy time (do not delete the previous release's assets immediately; keep several versions around).
worst_places.after: The fix has two parts and you need both. In the application: catch the error, retry once, and reload the page if the retry fails too. At deploy time: do not delete the previous release's assets straight away — keep the last few versions.

The article defers the explanation to another topic («Механика самих CORS-заголовков разбирается в топиках HTTP/REST и Security»), but files are read out of order, so the deferral does not help this reader.

worst_places.quote: Typical culprits: code inside a Docker container or on a mounted drive, where file system events are not propagated — cured by switching to polling (`server.watch.usePolling` in Vite, `watchOptions.poll` in Webpack, with the caveat that polling burns CPU).
worst_places.problem: 40 words with four items above B2 vocabulary in one breath: "culprits", "propagated", "cured by", "burns CPU" (plus "with the caveat that" as a connector and CPU unexpanded). The medical metaphor "culprits ... cured" is also a dead metaphor carried over from the RU «виновники ... лечится», where it reads naturally and in English reads as register noise. The sentence is doing real diagnostic work, so a reader who stalls on "propagated" loses the actual instruction.
worst_places.before: Typical culprits: code inside a Docker container or on a mounted drive, where file system events are not propagated — cured by switching to polling (`server.watch.usePolling` in Vite, `watchOptions.poll` in Webpack, with the caveat that polling burns CPU).
worst_places.after: The usual causes: code inside a Docker container, or on a mounted drive. In both cases the file system does not pass change events through to the watcher. The fix is to switch to polling — `server.watch.usePolling` in Vite, `watchOptions.poll` in Webpack. Note that polling keeps the processor busy all the time.

worst_places.problem: A code block that contains no code — only two comments. patterns: STRENGTH, and the habit most worth codifying from this zone: section headings are claims, not labels, and the first sentence delivers the verdict before any mechanism. «Тришейкинг — это доказательство, а не уборка», «Модуль — это узел графа, а не файл в папке», «`import()` — единственная точка разрыва графа», «Главная идея: dev и prod — два разных инструмента под одной обёрткой». The heading pre-loads the claim, the lead sentence states it plainly, and the caveats follow. Even the interview-answers file obeys it: every answer opens with the verdict («Нужен, но не по той причине, которую называют чаще всего», «Только динамический `import()`», «Потому что `splitChunks.chunks` по умолчанию `'async'`»). This is why C averages 4.9 — the highest score in the zone by a wide margin — and it is a genuine step up on older topics, which tend to name a section after its subject and warm up for a paragraph before answering.

STRENGTH: the zone sustains three supports for concept density that older topics use only sporadically. (1) One running example — the `shop-admin` panel with three routes, only `Analytics` heavy — is introduced in article 01 and every later article cuts, hashes, shakes and proxies that same app, so no article spends words re-establishing a scenario. (2) Nearly every major section carries one ASCII table or diagram, usually with a two-line caption that states the takeaway rather than repeating the table («первые три — про то, как быстрее сделать ту же работу; последние три — про то, как сделать её меньше»). (3) Every code block opens with a `// path/to/file` comment and is complete enough to read alone. Result: articles 02, 03 and 05 have zero theory walls, D averages 4.1 and E averages 4.3.

DEFECT, the #1 repeating one: the house habit is to explain the concept next to an acronym while never binding the letters to the words. ESM appears 118 times and CJS 92 times across the 18 files and neither is expanded once anywhere in the zone; the same holds for IIFE, AMD, UMD, CORS, AST, CDN, CI and SPA. The near-misses show it is a habit rather than an oversight: IIFE arrives as «IIFE-обёртка, которая прячет внутренности и отдаёт наружу один объект» (function explained, letters not), and article 02 puts a `CJS` heading directly above a sentence containing the words CommonJS without ever equating them. Fix is mechanical and local — one clause at first use per file — and it is the single highest-value pass available on this zone.

DEFECT: the EN version is systematically harder than the RU, not equally hard, and the mechanism is identifiable. RU keeps 2.4–6.4% of sentences over 28 words; EN runs 9.2–21.2% over 25. The translation faithfully preserves RU's colon-plus-em-dash-plus-parenthesis chaining and then spends ~19% more words inside the same frame, so a comfortable 28-word RU sentence lands as a 42-word EN one with two nested brackets (see the en/04 worst_place). On top of that sits a recurring register spike absent from the RU: "galling", "bluntness", "heresy", "quirk", "the tell", "invites drift", "ill-posed", "isomorphic", "culprits ... cured", "burns CPU", "pull on", "where to knock". F is the one criterion where this zone is not better than the older topics.

DEFECT: file 09 (the interview cheat sheet) is the only file in the zone with no table or diagram at all, and it is where the density failures concentrate — 28–29 long paragraphs and the zone's two worst sentences. The content is not new: answers 14, 15, 23 and 24 restate material that articles 04, 06 and 07 present as clean three-column tables, flattened here into 90-word semicolon chains with bold run-in labels. The fix costs nothing new, it reuses structures the zone already owns.
notes: Overall this is the strongest zone I would expect to see on the site and it should be the style-guide reference for C, D and E; verdict is targeted-fixes only because A (acronyms) and the EN sentence length are enumerable, local fixes, not a language pass. Two mechanical bugs: ru/08 line 48 has «Bandлер на Rust» — a Latin/Cyrillic mix, the only one in the zone (should be «Бандлер»); ru/05 line 233 is a code block containing only comments. The 128 inline English article titles in RU prose are a site-wide convention (rxjs RU does the same), so decide it globally rather than patching this topic. One thing worth preserving explicitly: the zone consistently timestamps volatile facts («на момент написания», «статус стоит проверять в документации») and even makes that a scored interview skill — it is a good habit and should not be edited out as hedging.
